comments.text: The Q-truck's stock, nine entries the shop reads through the table at $40CA: the icon's sprite frame, its colour, the price in Q tokens (BCD; $FF means it is worked out from the damage), the name in lower-case ASCII ending in 0, then the value to store and the address it goes to. In order: sub capability (75, sets $65), miniature lasers (25, $62 = 31), pursuit missiles (10, $59 = 31), smoke refill (5, $5A = $7F), side rear bolts (10, $64 on), armour replacement ($96F0 full), intercept missiles (15, $5B = 31), torpedoes (15, $63 = 31) and exit the q truck (0).
The word "cost " printed before an item's price.
The price of the item under the cursor, set by $447C and paid by $4406.
The addresses of the shop's entries, two bytes each, indexed by the cursor $40E8 (6 to $16 in steps of 2: the first three slots point at $4000 and $4001 and are not used).
The high bytes of the shop's entry addresses, read with $40CA.
The shop's cursor, 6 to $16 in steps of 2: which item faces the arrow.
The high-score table: nine entries of seven bytes, three letters (1-26 for A-Z, 27 a space) and a four-byte BCD score, best first. Offsets from $8844.
The second and third letters and the score of the first entry, addressed field by field when a new score is put in.
The first entry's third letter.
The first entry's score, four BCD bytes from $40EC to $40EF, compared with $9D-$A0 by $4236.
The first entry's score, second BCD byte.
The first entry's score, third BCD byte.
The first entry's score, last BCD byte.
The high-score table from its second entry on, which $4187 moves down a place to make room for a new score.

Empties the buffers ($284E) and writes the nine entries of the table into the character buffer from $E28C, two rows apart: the three letters (character $DA plus the letter) and the score's eight digits ($4270), then shows it ($0FC3).
The drawing loop of $4128, entered directly with $14/$15 already set: nine rows of letters and digits, then a redraw ($0FC3).

After the last life: silences the sound, dissolves the screen, draws the table, and finds the score's place ($4236). If it makes the table, moves the lower entries down, puts the score in with the name AAA and lets the player choose three letters: up and down step through A-Z (wrapping), right moves to the next letter, half a second apart ($1129).
Steps the letter under the cursor ($1D) to the next, Z back to A.
Steps the letter back, A round to Z.
Fixes this letter and moves to the next (three in all, counted by $90).
Compares the score $9D-$A0 with the table's entries in order ($8844); returns the place in $8F, or $FF when it is lower than all nine.
Writes the BCD byte in A as two digit characters ($86FA) at ($14),Y, moving Y on.

The Q-truck shop, opened by $0BF6 when the car is inside the truck. Saves the play screen ($42CE), dissolves the screen, puts back the road charset, shows the interior and runs the shop ($4381) from item $0E. On leaving, waits, flips the double buffer and puts the play screen back ($42E4).
Copies three pages of the character buffer ($E242) to the hidden screen ($7800 or $7C00), which is used as a store while the shop is open.
Copies the stored screen back into the character buffer, rebuilding the colour buffer from table $E782, clears colour memory $D800-$DAFF and redraws ($0FC3).
Points ($04) at the character buffer and ($06) at the hidden screen.
Points ($06) at the sprite pointers of the screen not being shown ($7BF8 or $7FF8).

Writes the zero-ended message at ($04) into the character buffer at $E38A, and shows it for a few seconds ($1129). Used for "get ready", "bad show james", "well done", "game over" and "congratulations".

Draws the panel, the icons ($4436) and the item name and price ($447C), then reads the joystick: up and down slide the column of icons to the next item ($43BD, $43E1), fire buys it ($4406). Leaves when fire is pressed on the exit.
Scrolls the icons down one place, a pixel a frame, and moves the cursor to the previous item; nothing at the first.
Scrolls the icons up one place and moves the cursor to the next item; nothing at the last.
Fire on an item (once per press, $3D). With a price of 0 it is the exit. Otherwise, if the Q tokens ($6A/$6B) cover the price, takes it off and stores the item's value at its address.
Puts seven item icons on the seven hardware sprites in a column at x $3C, 32 lines apart from $20, with each entry's frame and colour.
Prints the name of the item under the cursor and keeps its price in $40C9. For the armour the price is the damage: (255 - armour) / 8, capped by AND $17, plus 1. Then prints "cost" and the price.
Writes the zero-ended ASCII text at ($04) into ($14), adding $7A to each byte to make the character code (the character set holds its letters from $DB).
Entry into $44E1 that starts at the Y already set, so a caller can skip a header.
Fills 31 characters at ($14) with spaces.

Run once at start-up. Fills colour memory with 3 (cyan, multicolour off), $DB20-$DBE7 (the panel) with 1, and the four border columns of the play area with 0; clears the panel screen rows ($8300 page) and copies the panel's three rows of characters (31 each) ($8704, $8724, $8744) to $834B, $8373, $839B and their colours ($8764, $8784, $87A4) to colour memory; sets the panel's sprite pointers ($83F8-$83FF) to 12.

Ends both sprite lists, points the multiplexer at the first ($08, $B1), moves every sprite to y 0, unexpanded and multicolour, sets sprite multicolour 1 to white and 2 to black, and clears all 32 object slots.
Clears the 16 shots at $9A22 and gives each its own character definition, 8 bytes apart from $E1C2.
Zeros to the end of the overlay ($47FF).
